chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from 'Isa ibn Abi Mansur, from al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him say: Verily, Allah is Light in which there is no darkness, and Knowledge in which there is no ignorance, and Life in which there is no death.
ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of Light, Knowledge, and Life in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) articulates the concept of divine simplicity, asserting that God's attributes are not distinct entities added to His essence but are identical with it, thereby negating any multiplicity or composition in the Divine. By describing Allah as Light, Knowledge, and Life without their opposites, it reinforces the Shia theological stance against anthropomorphism and emphasizes the absolute purity and self-sufficiency of the Creator. This narration is foundational in understanding the nature of Tawhid (Oneness) as presented in Shaykh al-Saduq's al-Tawhid.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 13. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, on the `Isa ibn Abu Mansur, on the authority of Jabir al-Ju`fi, that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) said:
“Verily, Allah is Light as there is no darkness in Him, Allah is Knowledge as there is no ignorance in Him. And Allah is Life as there is no death in Him.”
